intent: Changed: sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 m, keeping the widened row (x = -0.024 to +0.024 m, 12 mm spacing, y = 0.04 m) that improved progress on all three tracks. Kept wheel track, wheel radius, body and mass so the race isolates the sensor footprint. Expected result: fewer line_loss_events on the slalom (from 2.0 toward 1.0 or lower) and somewhat higher slalom and s-bend progress, with the oval holding about 0.95 progress. I am considering wheel_track 0.10 m for yaw response if max_error stays at 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom with no change in steering oscillation, but I am not committing to it yet.
learning: Compare against iteration 1. If slalom line_loss_events fall and progress rises, the larger footprint helps signal on alternating bends, so keep 0.016. If slalom line losses stay at 2.0 and max_error still reaches 0.06, the limit is yaw response, so test wheel_track 0.10 m next. Check whether the oval keeps its 0.7 finish rate. Also check whether the larger sensor blurs the edge on the s-bend, which would show as higher rms_error.
rationale: Iteration 1 met the Integrator's first condition. Progress rose on all three tracks versus iteration 0: oval 0.176 to 0.952, s-bend 0.135 to 0.380, slalom 0.094 to 0.120. So the widened row (x = -0.024 to +0.024 m at y = 0.04 m) is kept. The Integrator's second condition (max_error still at 0.06 m with low steering oscillation) is not met. Steering oscillation rose on the s-bend (0.134 to 0.265) and sits at 0.20 on the slalom, so I am not reducing yaw inertia yet. The third condition does apply. Slalom line_loss_events is 2.0 in every slalom trial, and that track carries the most line-loss events. The Integrator's suggested fix is sensor_size 0.016 with the same positions, so I am taking it. A 16 mm footprint covers more of the 25 mm tape at the same sensor positions, which should give more signal per sensor when the robot is off-centre or alternating across the line. I am changing only sensor_size, so the race isolates this effect. I expect fewer slalom line-loss events and some progress gain on the slalom, with the oval unchanged or slightly better. Completion on the s-bend and slalom is still unlikely, so yaw response (wheel_track 0.10 m) remains the next candidate if max_error stays at the limit.
